ref.substituent_description: A bicyclic with a five-membered ring (N, CH, CH2, and two shared carbons) fused to a six-membered ring containing one N: the five-membered ring N bears Ac, the carbon next to that N bears EtOOC, and the next carbon is CH2. In the six-membered ring the N is separated from the fusion carbon (bonded to the Ac-N) by one CH, and the carbon adjacent to that ring N (on the other side) bears OMe.
ref.notes: Typeset reference-style structure. Three double bonds all in the six-membered ring (one C=N, two C=C). No carbonyl double bonds are drawn since Ac and EtOOC are written as labels.

wrong.substituent_description: A five-membered ring containing an N (bearing Ac) is fused to a six-membered circled pyridine-type ring that contains one N. EtOOC is on the five-membered ring carbon that is adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon (the one remote from N-Ac). In the six-membered ring, the N is separated from the N-bearing fusion carbon by one CH, and OMe is on the carbon directly next to that ring N, para to the fusion carbon that carries the N(Ac).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: The Ac label is written with a capital A and a smaller c, tilted along the bond.
wrong.notes: Handwritten on grey paper. No explicit double bonds; the six-membered ring has an aromatic circle.

correct.substituent_description: A six-membered ring with an inner circle and one ring N is fused to a five-membered ring containing an N bearing Ac. Going round the six-membered ring: fusion carbon bonded to N-Ac, CH, ring N, carbon bearing OMe (adjacent to the ring N), CH, fusion carbon bonded to the CH2 of the five-membered ring. The five-membered ring carbon next to N-Ac carries EtOOC.
correct.notes: Handwritten. Fused 6-5 bicycle (azaindoline type). Aromatic ring shown as a circle only, no explicit double bonds. Filled dots at some vertices are pen pressure, not charges.

ref.substituent_description: Bicyclic 5-6 fused system: a five-membered ring containing an N (top left) fused to a six-membered pyridine-type ring containing one ring N at the top right. The five-ring N carries Ac; the adjacent five-ring carbon carries EtOOC; the next five-ring carbon is an unsubstituted CH2 vertex. On the six-ring, the carbon directly next to the ring N (top right) carries OMe (pyridine N and OMe carbon are adjacent, 1,2 relationship).
ref.notes: Typeset drawing. Three double bonds in the six-membered ring: one C=C at the top-left next to the fusion, one C=N at the right, one C=C at the bottom. The five-membered ring has only single bonds. No stereo bonds drawn at the EtOOC-bearing carbon.

wrong.substituent_description: Fused bicyclic: a five-membered ring containing N (N bears Ac, attached to a ring-fusion carbon) fused to a six-membered ring drawn with an aromatic circle and one ring N. In the five-membered ring the carbon next to the other (lower) fusion carbon carries EtOOC; in the six-membered ring the carbon directly adjacent to the ring N (on the side away from the fusion carbon that is attached to N-Ac) carries OMe.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Ac is written with a capital-looking C, read as Ac
wrong.notes: Handwritten photo. Six-membered ring contains N at the position meta to the upper fusion carbon; OMe is on the carbon alpha to that N.

correct.substituent_description: Fused bicyclic: a six-membered ring containing one ring N and drawn with an aromatic circle, fused to a five-membered ring containing an N that carries Ac. In the six-ring, going round from the fusion carbon that is bonded to N(Ac): CH, ring N, C bearing OMe (adjacent to the ring N), CH, then the other fusion carbon. In the five-ring: N(Ac), the CH bearing EtOOC (adjacent to N(Ac)), a CH2 vertex, and the two fusion carbons.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: dark ink blobs at the vertex bearing EtOOC and at the vertex bearing OMe (not wedges)
correct.notes: No double bonds drawn other than the aromatic circle. The five-ring vertex between the EtOOC carbon and the fusion carbon is a plain CH2 vertex with no label.
